hints: Focus on what happens to the H-X bond as the halogen atom gets bigger down Group 17.
Remember that $\text{HI}$ decomposes on gentle heating while $\text{HCl}$ needs very strong heating, and that $\text{I}^-$ is a much stronger reducing agent than $\text{Cl}^-$.
Link weaker bonds to lower thermal stability, and stronger reducing power to easier oxidation of the halide, then pick the row that matches both trends.
walkthrough:
**Think About Thermal Stability and Bond Strength**

Thermal stability means how well $\text{HX}$ resists breaking apart into $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{X}_2$ on heating. It depends on H-X bond enthalpy.

$$\text{H-X bond strength: HCl > HBr > HI}$$

**Apply the Trend Down the Group**

Down the group the halogen atom gets larger, so orbital overlap gets poorer and the bond gets longer and weaker. A weaker bond needs less heat to break, so stability decreases.

$$\text{thermal stability: HF > HCl > HBr > HI}$$

**Think About Oxidation of the Halide**

Oxidation here means $\text{X}^-$ losing electrons to form $\text{X}_2$. Larger ions like $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ lose electrons more easily, so they are stronger reducing agents.

$$2\text{X}^- \rightarrow \text{X}_2 + 2e^-$$

**Combine Both Trends to Choose the Row**

Easier electron loss means easier to oxidise down the group, from $\text{HCl}$ (needs strong oxidant like concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ does not oxidise it) to $\text{HI}$ (easily oxidised). Easier to oxidise plus decreasing thermal stability matches only one row.

options.A: Half right and half wrong. It is true that hydrogen halides get easier to oxidise down the group, but thermal stability does not increase. Bond strength falls from HCl to HI, so stability decreases.
options.B: Both trends are reversed. Students sometimes confuse increasing atomic size with increasing stability, and confuse oxidising power of halogens (which decreases down the group) with ease of oxidation of halides (which increases).
options.C: Correct on both counts. Weaker H-X bonds down the group mean lower thermal stability, and larger halide ions lose electrons more readily so oxidation gets easier from HCl to HBr to HI.
options.D: Half right and half wrong. Thermal stability does decrease down the group, but it does not get more difficult to oxidise. Iodide is oxidised very easily to iodine, while chloride is very difficult to oxidise.
